summary: mcphub runs five parallel auth stacks (bearer key, its own OAuth token, better-auth session, JWT, guest) through one 100-line middleware chain, and two divergent authorization paths that disagree on `owner === undefined`. MCPRouter ships three credential kinds — better-auth session cookie, better-auth `apiKey` (`mcpr_` prefix), better-auth `mcp` plugin OAuth token — all verified by better-auth, all collapsing into one `Principal` discriminated union whose machine arm has `admin: false` as a *literal type*, so an admin-owned API key cannot be represented as admin. The single idea that makes it leaner: **authorization is a WHERE clause, never an if-statement.** One `visibleTo(principal, action, table)` SQL predicate is the only authz code that exists; `packages/core` never exports a raw Drizzle handle, so a new endpoint physically cannot read a row without a Principal — the divergence class mcphub has is unrepresentable. Secrets use one `seal`/`open` pair over a keyring with ID-based AAD, and upstream OAuth reuses the MCP SDK's `OAuthClientProvider` rather than re-implementing RFC 9728/8707/PKCE.

decisions.decision: Three credential kinds, one verifier, zero hand-rolled credential storage: better-auth core (session / email+password / GitHub / Google / genericOAuth OIDC), better-auth `apiKey` plugin (machines), better-auth `mcp` plugin (OAuth 2.1 AS for downstream MCP clients).
decisions.rationale: The plugins cover generation, hashing, expiry+cleanup, rate limiting, PKCE, RFC 8414/9728 metadata, DPoP and stateless token verification. What we still write is only: the Grant encoding, the scope intersection, the chokepoint, and the key-creation route that enforces subset escalation.
decisions.cost: ~110 LOC of config; we own no password, token or key storage code.
decisions.mcphub_contrast: Replaces middlewares/auth.ts:108-204 (five stacks), the plaintext BearerKey table (db/entities/BearerKey.ts:21) and its O(n) `safeCompare` scan over every enabled key (auth.ts:37-56), oauthServerService.ts, models/OAuth.ts and oauthService.ts entirely.

decisions.decision: Drop JWT, drop guest/`skipAuth`, drop tokens in query strings. Every request carries a session cookie or `Authorization: Bearer`.
decisions.rationale: A self-hosted multi-user hub has no anonymous tier, and mcphub's per-process random JWT secret (config/jwt.ts:4-14) silently breaks multi-replica. Query-string tokens leak into proxy logs — mcphub does it on `/api/logs/stream` and in `auth.ts:178-180`.
decisions.cost: The log/activity SSE streams must send the cookie (same-origin EventSource does) — no token param anywhere.
decisions.mcphub_contrast: Removes two of the five stacks and the `?token=` read path.

decisions.decision: CONFIRM `metadata.grant` and the `mcpr_` prefix. Correct two things: the grant is zod-parsed on every read and fails closed to deny, and the plugin's client-facing `/api/auth/api-key/*` endpoints are 404'd so keys can only be minted through `POST /api/keys`.
decisions.rationale: `enableMetadata: true` makes metadata writable by the key owner through the plugin's own endpoints, so an unblocked create route lets a member self-issue `{scope:{kind:'all'}}`. The prefix earns its keep because it is what disambiguates an API key from an OAuth access token on the same `Authorization: Bearer` header.
decisions.mcphub_contrast: mcphub scopes bearer keys only on MCP routes (sseService.ts:202-315) and leaves the dashboard API grant implicit in `kind==='system' && accessType==='all'` (auth.ts:61-66).

decisions.decision: An API key NEVER implies admin — enforced by two structural facts, not a check: `disableSessionForAPIKeys: true` in the apiKey plugin config, and `admin: false` as a *literal type* in the machine arm of the `Principal` union.
decisions.rationale: Without the flag, better-auth's apiKey plugin mints a mock session for a key, so `getSession()` would return the owner and our session→admin branch would hand an admin's key full admin. With the literal type, `{via:'apikey', admin:true}` is a compile error — no runtime check can be forgotten.
decisions.cost: Zero. Two lines and a type.
decisions.mcphub_contrast: mcphub's auth.ts:132-141 explicitly sets `isAdmin:true` for a system bearer key, which is the exact hazard.

decisions.decision: Two roles: `admin` and `member`. `role` is a better-auth `additionalFields` entry with `input: false`; the first user created becomes admin via a `databaseHooks.user.create.before` count.
decisions.rationale: The only genuinely distinct capability set in a team hub is 'can change things that affect everyone' (users, system settings, key policy, override on any resource); read-only sharing is already expressible as `visibility: shared` plus `grant.invoke:false`. `input:false` is load-bearing — without it a signup payload can set `role:'admin'`.

decisions.decision: THE CHOKEPOINT: `visibleTo(principal, action, table): SQL`, composed with `grantFilter(grant, table): SQL`, is the only authorization code. Every read is a SELECT with that predicate; every write is an UPDATE/DELETE with it in the WHERE, and 0 affected rows → 404, never 403.
decisions.rationale: Two functions (a boolean guard and a query filter) is exactly how mcphub got dataService.ts:6-28 disagreeing with DaoConfigService:171; one SQL form cannot diverge from itself. Returning 404 rather than 403 also gives an invisible resource and a nonexistent one identical responses, matching the `ToolUnavailableError` doctrine (mcpService.ts:2654).

decisions.decision: Structural bypass prevention (committing to ONE mechanism): `packages/core` never exports the Drizzle handle. The package `exports` map publishes only `./index.js`, and `index.ts` exports `scoped(p: Principal)` — repositories that already embed the predicate. Backed by one regression test that enumerates `app.routes`.
decisions.rationale: The ESM subpath-exports map is a platform feature, not a lint rule someone can `// eslint-disable`; a new endpoint cannot obtain a queryable handle without producing a Principal first. The route-enumeration test is the belt, not the braces.
decisions.cost: Any legitimately unscoped operation (migrations, the embedding sync worker) needs an explicit `systemPrincipal()` with a comment naming why.

decisions.decision: Resources carry `owner_id NOT NULL REFERENCES user(id)` plus `visibility: 'private'|'shared'|'public'`; seeded/system resources are owned by the bootstrap admin.
decisions.rationale: mcphub's whole divergence is one branch over `owner === undefined` (DaoConfigService:171 treats it as visible to everyone, dataService.ts does not) and `group.visibility == null` opening a route to any authenticated caller (utils/groupAccess.ts:6). A NOT NULL column deletes the branch rather than reconciling it.

decisions.decision: One `seal`/`open` pair over an env keyring (`MCPR_SECRET_KEYS=v2:…,v1:…`, first = active) with AES-256-GCM and ID-based AAD, used for upstream env, headers, upstream OAuth client info/tokens and per-user credential bindings. Missing key = refuse to boot, printing a paste-ready generated line. Never auto-create a key file.
decisions.rationale: mcphub encrypts only credential bindings (credentialBindingService.ts:18-118) and leaves upstream OAuth tokens, client secrets and issued tokens plaintext (oauthSettingsStore.ts:107-168); its auto-created `<settings>.credentials.key` is the same silent-divergence failure as its random JWT secret. AAD on IDs rather than names (mcphub uses `[serverName,username]`) means a rename does not brick decryption.

decisions.decision: The AsyncLocalStorage store is observability-only. Core authorization functions take `principal` as an explicit parameter and an eslint `no-restricted-imports` forbids the context getter inside `packages/core/src/{authz,db}/**`. `.enterWith()` is already banned by the observability agent's rule; we do not duplicate it.
decisions.rationale: mcphub's leak (userContextService.ts:28,38) is dangerous precisely because authz reads the ALS; if ours leaks, the blast radius is a mislabeled log line. Authorization that takes its principal as an argument cannot inherit the wrong one.

interfaces.name: Grant / Scope / Principal
interfaces.notes: Core owns the TYPE; packages/server owns the verification. Note the literal `admin: false` in the machine arm — that is the whole 'a key is never admin' enforcement. No `role` field: `admin` is already resolved, and ownership uses `userId`.

interfaces.name: intersectScope — route scope ∩ grant scope
interfaces.notes: Reproduces mcphub's GHSA-454m-4vm6-842f full-containment rule (sseService.ts:228-302) as one table-driven function instead of scattered checks. Runs at the HTTP edge BEFORE any engine call; `null` → 403. `members()` is injected so core stays DB-agnostic here and the function is unit-testable as a pure truth table.

interfaces.name: authenticate — the single edge verifier
interfaces.notes: The ONLY place a Principal is constructed from a request. ~70 LOC replacing mcphub's five-stack chain. Note: the API key is read from `Authorization: Bearer` only — never `x-api-key` — so there is exactly one header to reason about, and the `mcpr_` prefix is what routes between the two bearer verifiers.

interfaces.name: THE CHOKEPOINT — visibleTo + scoped()
interfaces.notes: `raw` is module-private and `packages/core/package.json` publishes only `"exports": { ".": "./dist/index.js" }`. packages/server cannot import a queryable handle. Every read AND write goes through the same predicate, so there is no second authz form to diverge. 0 rows affected on a write → 404, identical to a nonexistent id.

interfaces.name: seal / open — the one crypto helper
interfaces.notes: One pair, four call sites: upstream `env`, upstream `headers`, upstream OAuth (client info + tokens), per-user credential bindings. Stored as a single opaque `text` column everywhere — the schema agent needs no bytea, no JSON shape. `${VAR}` expansion from process.env still happens at connect time, on the *opened* plaintext.

interfaces.name: better-auth configuration
interfaces.notes: The three load-bearing lines are marked. `disableSessionForAPIKeys` and `input:false` are security controls, not preferences — a reviewer should treat changing either as a CVE. Social/OIDC providers are only registered when their env vars exist, so there is no dead config for a value that never changes.

interfaces.name: Auth route table
interfaces.notes: `session` = cookie principal. `admin` = `principal.admin === true`, which only a session can ever be. `principal` = any of the three. Everything under /api except /api/auth and the well-knowns is behind `requireAuth`; the route-enumeration test below asserts that mechanically.
interfaces.sketch:
METHOD  PATH                                          AUTH            NOTES
ALL     /api/auth/*                                   (handler)       better-auth; sign-in/out, social, OIDC callback
ALL     /api/auth/api-key/*                           BLOCKED 404     plugin's client key CRUD is not reachable
GET     /.well-known/oauth-authorization-server        public          mcp plugin (RFC 8414)
GET     /.well-known/oauth-protected-resource         public          mcp plugin (RFC 9728) — target of WWW-Authenticate
GET     /.well-known/oauth-protected-resource/mcp/*   public          per-endpoint variant; audience = the /mcp/... URL
GET|POST /oauth2/authorize                            session         mcp plugin; unauth -> 302 /login?next=
POST    /oauth2/token                                 public          PKCE S256 required; audience bound to `resource`
GET     /oauth2/userinfo                              oauth token     mcp plugin
GET     /consent                                      session         SPA route (real React page, not an injected shell
                                                                       like mcphub oauthServerController.ts:434-470)

GET     /api/me                                       principal       { user, admin, grant, via } — the UI reads capability from here
GET     /api/keys                                     session         own keys; admin sees all
POST    /api/keys                                     session         body { name, grant, expiresIn? }; grant MUST be a subset of
                                                                       creator's reachable set (verified via scoped(p).servers.list());
                                                                       calls auth.api.createApiKey server-side; plaintext shown ONCE
DELETE  /api/keys/:id                                 session         owner or admin
GET     /api/users                                    admin
PATCH   /api/users/:id                                admin           { role?, disabled? } — cannot demote the last admin
DELETE  /api/users/:id                                admin           reassigns owned resources to the acting admin
PUT     /api/:kind/:slug/share                        session(manage)  { visibility, userIds[] } -> resource_share rows

POST    /api/servers/:slug/oauth/start                session(manage)  -> { authorizeUrl }; mints upstream_oauth_state row
GET     /oauth/callback                               session + state  upstream-client callback; state row must match session.userId;
                                                                       10-min TTL, single use. (mcphub's is PUBLIC.)
DELETE  /api/servers/:slug/oauth                      session          revokes the caller's own upstream tokens
PUT     /api/servers/:slug/credentials                session          write-only sealed slots; GET returns { slot, hasValue }

POST    /mcp | /mcp/smart | /mcp/{g,s}/:slug          principal        401 + WWW-Authenticate: Bearer resource_metadata="…", scope="mcp:invoke"
                                                                       403 + error="insufficient_scope" when intersectScope() -> null
GET     /api/logs/stream, /api/activity/stream        session          cookie-authenticated EventSource — NO ?token= (mcphub logService.ts:82)

interfaces.name: Upstream OAuth client (MCPRouter -> remote MCP server)
interfaces.notes: Distinct from the mcp plugin, which makes us an AS. Here we are a CLIENT. RFC 9728 discovery, RFC 8707 `resource`, PKCE and refresh-on-401 all come from the SDK's `auth()` / transport pair — we only implement storage and the human hand-off. ~150 LOC.

interfaces.name: Tables I need (schema agent owns the DDL)
interfaces.notes: better-auth's CLI generates `user`(+role,+disabled), `session`, `account`, `verification`, `apikey`, and the mcp/oauth-provider set (`oauthApplication`, `oauthAccessToken`, `oauthRefreshToken`, `oauthConsent`) into our Drizzle schema file — we commit them and they get real migration files like everything else. We add four tables and three columns.
interfaces.sketch:
resource_share(resource_kind 'server'|'group', resource_id uuid, user_id text, created_at) PK(kind,id,user_id)
  -- the `shared` visibility list; the only table visibleTo() joins.

upstream_oauth(server_id uuid, user_id text NULL, client_info text NULL, tokens text NULL,
               authorize_url text NULL, updated_at) UNIQUE(server_id, user_id NULLS NOT DISTINCT)
  -- client_info/tokens are Sealed strings. user_id NULL = shared service account.

upstream_oauth_state(state text PK, server_id uuid, user_id text, code_verifier text,
                     created_at, expires_at) -- 10-min TTL, single use, swept hourly.

credential_binding(server_id uuid, user_id text, slot text, value text, updated_at)
  UNIQUE(server_id, user_id, slot) -- value is Sealed; write-only from the API.

COLUMNS on servers AND groups:
  owner_id text NOT NULL REFERENCES "user"(id) ON DELETE RESTRICT
  visibility text NOT NULL DEFAULT 'private' CHECK (visibility IN ('private','shared','public'))
  -- NOT NULL is the fix for mcphub's divergence (dataService.ts:6-28 vs DaoConfigService:171)
COLUMNS on servers:
  env text NULL, headers text NULL          -- Sealed strings, not jsonb.
INDEX: (owner_id, visibility) on both; (resource_id, user_id) on resource_share.

interfaces.name: The regression net (2 test files, ~180 LOC)
interfaces.notes: Not the primary mechanism — the exports map is (D7). These fail loudly when someone works around it.

deferred.add_when: someone needs a human who can see the hub but own nothing — today that is a member with zero owned resources. Upgrade: one enum value + one branch in visibleTo().

deferred.item: Teams/groups-of-users as share targets (resource_share currently holds user ids only)
deferred.add_when: the share list on a resource routinely exceeds ~10 users. The table already has a `resource_kind` column; add a `principal_kind` and one join.
a downstream client asks for sender-constrained tokens, or a security review flags bearer replay. Config-only change.
the team exceeds ~50 users or an IdP mandates it. Today `PATCH /api/users/:id {disabled:true}` plus the session `create.before` hook covers off-boarding.

deferred.item: Per-key IP allowlist and per-key audit surfacing
deferred.add_when: keys leave the building (CI runners, partner integrations). The apiKey plugin already records the key id on every call; observability owns the join.

deferred.item: KMS/HSM-backed key wrapping under the existing `mcpr.v1.<kid>` envelope
deferred.add_when: compliance requires keys never sit in env, or row counts make full-table reseal too slow. The envelope format already carries the kid.

risks: better-auth 1.7.5 option names are taken from its docs, not from installed types — `disableSessionForAPIKeys`, `enableMetadata` and `mcp({oidcConfig})` are load-bearing and must be confirmed against the installed d.ts on day one; if `disableSessionForAPIKeys` is absent, the fallback is to never call getSession() when an Authorization header is present.

`auth.api.getMcpSession()` must expose the token's `resource`/audience; if it does not, we read the audience from the introspected token claims ourselves — otherwise OAuth grants silently widen to the whole hub.

The exports-map chokepoint holds only while `packages/core` has one entry point; adding a `./db` subpath export for any reason (tests, the migration CLI) reopens the bypass. The route-coverage test does not catch that — the `no raw db handle` test does.

Per-user upstream OAuth means N token sets per server and N upstream runtimes; the fail-closed rule (no fallback to the shared token) will produce `oauth_required` for users who expected the admin's connection to just work. This is correct and will be reported as a bug.

`resource_share` joined via EXISTS on every list query is fine at team scale but is an uncorrelated subquery per row if the planner misjudges; if server/group counts reach 10^4 the predicate becomes a lateral join or a materialized visibility view.
security: Identical response for hidden and nonexistent: writes gated in the WHERE return 0 rows -> 404, matching mcphub's ToolUnavailableError doctrine (mcpService.ts:2654) at the resource layer too. No existence oracle.

Enable/disable enforced at CALL time, not only list time: `visibleTo(p,'invoke',...)` is evaluated on the tools/call path with the same predicate as tools/list, so mcphub's CVE fix (afcc72f) is structural here rather than a second gate inside findToolOnServer (:3388).

Privilege escalation on key creation: `POST /api/keys` verifies the requested grant is a subset of the creator's own reachable set via `scoped(creator).servers.list()` before calling createApiKey. A member cannot mint a key wider than themselves.
`role` is `input:false` and `owner_id` is server-assigned from the principal on insert — neither is ever read from a request body.

Upstream OAuth callback requires a live session whose user matches the server-side state row, and the state row is single-use with a 10-minute TTL. mcphub's `/oauth/callback` is public. Redirect target after callback is a fixed internal path, never a query parameter.

SSRF validation on every upstream URL and every redirect hop, including OAuth metadata/authorize/token fetches — the shared `ssrfGuardedFetch`, with no admin-owned bypass (mcphub bypasses it for admin-owned servers, mcpService.ts:1382-1396; an admin-owned server config is still attacker-influenced via the marketplace).
No secret is ever returned by an API: sealed columns surface as `{ hasValue: boolean }`, and an API key's plaintext is shown exactly once at creation.

No token in any query string, no JWT, no anonymous tier. 401 carries `WWW-Authenticate: Bearer resource_metadata="…", scope="…"`; insufficient scope at runtime is 403 with `error="insufficient_scope"`.

The ALS store is observability-only; every authorization decision takes its Principal as an explicit parameter, so an ALS leak cannot become an authorization bug (contrast userContextService.ts:28,38 feeding authz).
Boot refuses to start without `MCPR_SECRET_KEYS` and `BETTER_AUTH_SECRET`. No auto-generated key file, no per-process random secret.
phase: v1 / MVP — buildable in parallel with the schema agent; the only cross-agent contracts are the four tables plus three columns listed above, and the exported `visibleTo` / `grantFilter` predicates that the smart-routing agent must compose into the pgvector query (scope pushed into SQL, never filtered after LIMIT).
